name: issue_867_comfort_family_reactive_mild_day_floor_breach
description: Issue #867 / #1066 (Design D nearest-edge arming, docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md section 6f). Same shape as issue_858_comfort_family_reactive_floor_breach.json but for DAY_TYPE_MILD (classifier hvac_mode=off). The original #867 defect was a reactive-check guard that returned early whenever classification.hvac_mode was 'off' (warm and mild days); that guard no longer exists, and the check now runs for every day type and keys off the selector. First reading below the floor (06:15, 65F vs 66F) must arm heat immediately, so the switch lands by 06:15.
notes: Occupant impact: on a mild day (the classifier recommends HVAC off) a house drifting below the comfort floor must still get heat on the first reading below it, not after the next ~30-minute cycle.

Why a ceiling companion was not added: Design D is symmetric, but a mild-day house that has no heat armed is already guarding the ceiling via the default edge; the cool-side reactive path is covered by issue_858_comfort_family_reactive_ceiling_breach.json and issue_1066_heat_day_mirror_cool_armed_when_above_ceiling.json.

Classification fields: day_type=mild with hvac_mode=off, windows_recommended=false match classifier.py for DAY_TYPE_MILD (never hand-set). The assertion time bounds are the first breach reading (06:15).

(a) Scenario effectiveness: reintroducing a reactive-check guard on classification.hvac_mode (the #867 defect) returns early on every tick of this scenario, so comfort_family_switch_by never fires (no second classification event). With nearest-edge arming deleted (origin/main) a mild day is not natively heating, so heat is against-grain and needs the deadband breach, recency and a 90 s sustain across two evaluations; the first breach reading (06:15) would not switch, so comfort_family_switch_by(heating, 06:15) and the final-state assertions fail.
(b) Docs<->production alignment: docs/08 section 6f ('The day type is not an input to the arming decision'; reactive evaluation on every temperature change).

(c) Occupant outcome if this test fails to catch a regression: a mild-day house cools below its comfort floor with no heat for up to 30 minutes per missed cycle (the pattern that recurred after #858 first shipped).

events.note: Mild-day classification (hvac_mode=off, as classifier.py derives for DAY_TYPE_MILD). The ONLY classification event; everything after is driven by temp_update alone.
First reading below the floor: 65F, 1F below comfort_heat(66). Floor breach: the reactive check arms heat on this very reading.

assertions.reason: Baseline: mild day, indoor within band -- comfort band arms normally, even though the day's native recommendation is hvac_mode=off.
Issue #867 / #1066: the switch to heating lands on the first breach reading (06:15) on a day type whose classification.hvac_mode is 'off', driven entirely by the reactive temperature-tick path.
Final engine state confirms heating is armed, not merely an emitted event.
The commanded mode is a real climate service call at comfort_heat, not merely an internal flag.

verdict.summary: A floor breach on a mild (hvac_mode=off) day arms heat on the first reactive temperature tick (Issue #867, tightened for Issue #1066).
verdict.observed_behavior: Single classification event at 06:00 (mild/off); the 65F reading at 06:15 switches the family to heating and commands heat.
verdict.expected_behavior: Reactive applicability is decided by the armed band and the selector, never by the classifier's native hvac_mode recommendation.
